note: Original prep content written for MGA. No questions are copied from LeetCode, GeeksforGeeks or any company. Links come only from resources.json.

dsa_topics.name: Arrays and strings
patterns: Single pass with running state (max, min, count)
checklist: Find the second-largest value in one pass
Answer many 'sum of a range' queries quickly
Check whether two strings are anagrams

dsa_topics.name: Hashing (maps and sets)
patterns: Complement lookup (find a pair with a target sum)
checklist: Find the first non-repeating character
Group words that are anagrams of each other
Explain average vs worst-case hash map cost

dsa_topics.name: Two pointers and sliding window
patterns: Variable window that grows and shrinks with a condition
checklist: Longest substring with at most K distinct characters
Remove duplicates from a sorted array in place
Max sum of any K consecutive elements

dsa_topics.name: Sorting and binary search
patterns: Know merge sort and quicksort and their costs
Binary search on the answer (smallest X that works)
checklist: Find the first and last position of a value in sorted data
Find the minimum capacity to ship packages in D days
Explain why binary search needs a monotonic condition

dsa_topics.name: Linked lists
patterns: Detect a cycle with fast/slow pointers
checklist: Reverse a list iteratively and recursively
Find the middle node in one pass
Remove the N-th node from the end

dsa_topics.name: Stacks and queues
checklist: Validate a bracket string
For each day, find days until a warmer temperature
Implement a queue using two stacks

dsa_topics.name: Recursion and backtracking
patterns: Prune early when a partial answer can't work
checklist: Generate all subsets of a set
Place N queens on a board
Explain the call stack and its space cost

dsa_topics.name: Binary trees and BSTs
patterns: Return values up the tree (height, diameter)
BST property for search and validation
checklist: Compute the height and diameter of a tree
Check whether a tree is a valid BST
Find the lowest common ancestor of two nodes

dsa_topics.name: Heaps and priority queues
patterns: Two heaps for a running median
checklist: Find the K most frequent words
Merge K sorted lists
Explain heap push/pop cost

dsa_topics.name: Graphs: BFS, DFS, topological sort
patterns: BFS for shortest path in unweighted graphs
DFS for connected components and cycle detection
checklist: Count islands in a grid
Order courses given prerequisites
Find the shortest number of moves in a grid maze

dsa_topics.name: Greedy algorithms
patterns: Take the locally best choice and argue why it's safe
checklist: Pick the maximum number of non-overlapping meetings
Find the minimum number of platforms for trains
Explain when greedy fails and DP is needed

dsa_topics.name: Dynamic programming
patterns: Define the state and the transition
checklist: Count ways to climb N steps taking 1 or 2 at a time
Longest common subsequence of two strings
0/1 knapsack and its space optimisation

dsa_topics.name: Shortest paths, union-find, MST
patterns: Kruskal / Prim for minimum spanning trees
checklist: Cheapest route between two cities with weighted roads
Detect whether adding an edge creates a cycle
Explain why Dijkstra fails with negative edges

dsa_topics.name: Tries and bit manipulation
patterns: Prefix tree for word search and autocomplete
checklist: Implement insert/search/startsWith on a trie
Find the single number that appears once when others appear twice
Count set bits in an integer

oop: Encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction with a code example each
Common patterns: singleton, factory, strategy, observer
os: Memory: paging, segmentation, virtual memory, page replacement
dbms: Normalisation (1NF to BCNF) with an example
Indexing: B-trees and when an index helps
networking: What happens when you type a URL
HTTP methods, status codes, HTTPS/TLS basics
system_design: Design a URL shortener end to end
sql: Window functions: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, running totals
Indexes and reading a query plan

topics: Profit and loss, simple and compound interest

aptitude_note: Many campus and off-campus online assessments for freshers in India include an aptitude section, but not all do. Check the posting or the test invite.

oa_formats.name: Coding round
oa_formats.what: Usually 2 to 4 problems in 60 to 120 minutes on an online judge. Hidden test cases decide the score, and partial credit for passing some cases is common.
prepare: Practise with a timer: about 25 minutes per medium problem
Read the constraints first; they tell you the complexity you need
Write the brute force, then optimise
Test edge cases: empty input, one element, duplicates, large values

oa_formats.name: CS fundamentals MCQs
oa_formats.what: Multiple-choice questions on OOP, OS, DBMS, networks and predicting the output of short programs.
prepare: Revise one core subject per day using the topic lists below
Practise output-prediction questions in your main language

oa_formats.name: Aptitude and reasoning
oa_formats.what: Timed quantitative, logical and verbal sections, often with a fixed time per section.
prepare: Learn the standard formulas, then do timed sets
Skip and return: don't spend 3 minutes on one question

oa_formats.name: SQL round
oa_formats.what: Write queries against a given schema: joins, aggregation and sometimes window functions. Common for data and backend roles.
prepare: Practise joins and GROUP BY until they're automatic
Learn ROW_NUMBER / RANK for 'top N per group' questions
Say your assumptions about NULLs and duplicates

oa_formats.name: Debugging or code-reading round
oa_formats.what: Find and fix bugs in given code, or explain what it does.
prepare: Read code top-down before changing anything
Check off-by-one errors, null handling and integer overflow first
Explain your fix and how you'd test it

oa_formats.name: Take-home assignment
oa_formats.what: A small project to finish in 2 to 7 days. More common at startups.
prepare: Clarify scope and deadline in writing
Ship a working core before extras
Add a README with setup steps, decisions and trade-offs, plus a few tests

questions: Tell me about a team project where one member wasn't contributing. What did you do?
Describe a time you helped a teammate get unstuck.
Tell me about something you built end to end. Which decisions were yours?
Describe a time you noticed a problem nobody asked you to fix. What happened?
Tell me about a technology you had to learn quickly for a project. How did you go about it?
What's something you learned recently outside your coursework?
Tell me about a project that didn't go as planned. What would you do differently?
Describe a bug that took you a long time to find. How did you find it?
Describe a time you disagreed with a teammate about how to build something. How was it resolved?
Why this role, and why now?
Where do you want to be in two years, and how does this job help?

star_tip: Answer with STAR: the Situation, your Task, the Actions you took (say 'I', not 'we'), and the Result, with a number if you have one.

projects.title: URL shortener with click analytics
projects.pitch: A service that turns long links into short codes, redirects fast and shows click counts per day.
milestones: Design the schema and short-code generation; write down how you avoid collisions
Build create/redirect endpoints with input validation
Add a cache for hot links and measure redirect latency before and after
Record clicks and expose a daily-stats endpoint
Write unit and API tests; package with Docker
Write a README with an architecture diagram and the trade-offs you made

projects.title: Real-time team chat
projects.pitch: Rooms, messages and online presence, with login and message history.
milestones: Sign-up and login with hashed passwords and sessions or tokens
Create rooms and send messages over WebSockets
Store and page through message history
Show who is online using a fast key-value store
Build the React UI with loading and error states
Deploy with Docker and document how to run it

projects.title: Background job processor
projects.pitch: An API accepts jobs (for example, resizing images); workers process them from a queue and report status.
milestones: Define the job API and a status table
Publish jobs to a message queue; build a worker that consumes them
Add retries with backoff and a dead-letter queue
Expose metrics (jobs processed, failures, latency) and a simple dashboard
Run producer, workers and database with Docker Compose
Load-test with 1,000 jobs and write up what broke and how you fixed it

projects.title: Ship a 3-service app with CI/CD on Kubernetes
projects.pitch: Take a small app (frontend, API, database) and deploy it the way a real team would.
milestones: Containerise each service with small images
Write Kubernetes manifests: deployments, services, config and secrets
Set up a pipeline that tests, builds and deploys on every push
Provision the cluster or VM with infrastructure-as-code
Add health checks, logs and basic alerts
Document a rollback and practise it once

projects.title: Product catalog web app
projects.pitch: Search, filter and paginate a product list from a public API, with a cart and good performance.
milestones: Set up a typed project and fetch products from a public API
Build search, filters and pagination that sync to the URL
Add a cart with state management and persistence
Handle loading, empty and error states; make it accessible
Write component tests
Measure and improve load performance; note the numbers in the README

projects.title: Sales analytics dashboard
projects.pitch: Take a public retail dataset, model it, and build a dashboard that answers 5 business questions.
milestones: Pick a public dataset and write down 5 business questions
Clean the data and document every assumption
Write SQL for each question: joins, aggregation, window functions
Build the dashboard with filters and clear chart titles
Add one statistical check (for example, is a difference significant?)
Write a one-page summary of findings with recommendations

projects.title: Daily ETL pipeline for public data
projects.pitch: Pull a public dataset on a schedule, clean it, load it into a warehouse table and track data quality.
milestones: Choose a public source that allows reuse and note its licence
Extract and store raw files by date
Transform with clear, tested cleaning steps
Load into a database with idempotent upserts
Add data-quality checks and a failure alert
Schedule it and write a README with the data flow
stretch: Rewrite the transform in a distributed engine

projects.title: Text classifier with an API
projects.pitch: Train a model to classify short texts (for example, support tickets by topic) and serve it behind an API.
milestones: Pick a labelled public dataset and set a baseline
Train and compare two models; report precision and recall
Analyse errors and improve one thing
Serve the model with an API and input validation
Track experiments and version the model
Containerise and document how to reproduce the results
stretch: A small UI for labelling new data

projects.title: Question answering over your own documents
projects.pitch: Upload documents and ask questions; answers quote the passage they came from.
milestones: Split documents into passages and index them for search
Retrieve the best passages for a question
Generate an answer that cites the passage, and refuse when nothing matches
Build an evaluation set of 30 questions and measure accuracy
Serve it behind an API with rate limits
Write up cost, latency and failure cases

projects.title: Habit tracker Android app
projects.pitch: Track daily habits with reminders, streaks and offline storage.
milestones: Design screens and the data model
Store habits locally and show streaks
Add reminders with notifications
Sync to a small backend API
Write unit tests for streak logic
Publish a test build and record a demo video

projects.title: Cross-platform expense splitter app
projects.pitch: Split bills in a group, track who owes whom and settle up, on Android and iOS from one codebase.
milestones: Model groups, expenses and balances
Build the add-expense and balances screens
Add login and sync to a backend
Write tests for the balance-settling logic
Handle offline edits and conflicts
Ship a test build and write the README

projects.title: Test automation suite for a public demo app
projects.pitch: Write a test plan and an automated UI + API test suite for a public practice web app, running in CI.
milestones: Write a test plan with cases for the main flows
Automate 10 UI tests with a page-object structure
Automate API tests with assertions on status and schema
Run everything in CI on every push
Report flaky tests and fix their causes
Publish an HTML report and a README

projects.title: Authentication service with roles
projects.pitch: Sign-up, login, token refresh and role-based access, built carefully and tested.
milestones: Store users with salted password hashes
Issue short-lived access tokens and refresh tokens
Add roles and protect endpoints by role
Rate-limit login attempts and log security events
Write tests for every auth path, including failures
Document the threat model and what you'd add next

projects.title: GraphQL API for a course catalog
projects.pitch: Courses, instructors and reviews exposed through a typed GraphQL API with pagination.
milestones: Design the schema and database tables
Implement queries with cursor pagination
Add mutations with validation
Fix N+1 queries with batching and measure the difference
Write resolver tests
Document example queries in the README

projects.title: Hostel expense splitter for iPhone
projects.pitch: A native iOS app where flatmates add shared expenses (chai, groceries, electricity) and see who owes whom, even offline.
milestones: Model groups, members and expenses in Swift value types and write down the rounding rule for uneven splits
Build the list and add-expense screens and show a validation message for empty or negative amounts
Persist data on the device and show that the app reopens with the same balances after being force-quit
Sync with a small REST backend and show a clear state when the network is down
Write unit tests for the split and settle-up logic, including a case that does not divide evenly
Record a short screen capture and a README that lists what you would change before a store submission
stretch: Simplify debts so the fewest payments settle the group
Export a month summary as a shareable text

projects.title: Vulnerable web app: find, exploit and fix
projects.pitch: Build a deliberately weak small web app on your own machine, document each flaw, then fix it and prove the fix with a test.
milestones: Build a small app with login, a search box and a profile page, running only on localhost
Plant and document three flaws (for example SQL injection, stored XSS, broken access control) with a step-by-step reproduction for each
Fix every flaw and add a regression test that fails on the old code and passes on the new
Add security headers, input validation and rate limiting on login, and show the before and after responses
Scan your own dependencies for known vulnerabilities and write up what you upgraded and why
Write a short report in the style of a penetration-test finding: impact, evidence, fix, residual risk
stretch: Threat-model the app with a data-flow diagram
Add an audit log that records failed logins

projects.title: Monsoon rainfall: trends and a simple forecast
projects.pitch: Use a public rainfall dataset for a few districts to test whether the monsoon is changing and how well a simple model predicts it.
milestones: Load a public dataset, document its source and licence in the README, and list the missing values you found
Clean the data in pandas and write down every assumption you made when filling or dropping gaps
State a hypothesis and test it (for example, mean June-September rainfall in two decades differs) with the test, the p-value and what it does not prove
Plot trends with uncertainty bands and a chart that a non-technical reader can follow
Fit a baseline and one regression model, split by year not randomly, and report the error of each on the held-out years
Write a one-page conclusion that separates what the data shows from what it cannot show
stretch: Compare two districts with a confidence interval on the difference
Check for outliers caused by sensor errors

projects.title: Kirana stock dashboard in Vue
projects.pitch: A single-page app where a shop owner tracks stock, sees low-stock items and a daily sales summary on a phone-sized screen.
milestones: Set up the project with TypeScript and define the types for items, stock movements and sales
Build the stock list with search, sort and a low-stock highlight using components with typed props
Add a form to record stock in and out with validation and clear error messages
Fetch data from a small mock REST API and handle loading, error and empty states
Write component tests for the form and the low-stock logic
Make it usable at 360px width and deploy a static build; note the Lighthouse scores you got
stretch: Rebuild one screen in Angular and write what differed
Add an offline cache so the list opens without network

projects.title: College club event portal in Django
projects.pitch: A web app where a college club posts events, students register, and organisers see attendance and export the list.
milestones: Design models for events, registrations and roles; draw the ER diagram and justify the constraints
Build event list, detail and registration pages with Django forms and server-side validation
Add login with separate permissions for students and organisers, and show a student failing to open an organiser page
Expose a small JSON API for events and write tests that cover registration limits and duplicates
Add an admin view with attendance export and show one query you optimised with select_related
Containerise with Docker and write setup steps another student can follow in 10 minutes
stretch: Email confirmation using a console backend in development
Port one view to Flask and compare the code

projects.title: Payment ledger with Spring Boot and Kafka
projects.pitch: Two Spring Boot services: one takes UPI-style transfer requests, the other updates account balances from events, with no double-credit on retries.
milestones: Define the event schema and the account tables, and write down which service owns which data
Build the transfer service with an idempotency key so the same request twice creates one transfer
Publish transfer events to a Kafka topic and consume them in the ledger service with manual offset commits
Prove with a test that replaying the same event does not credit twice
Add a dead-letter topic for events that fail, and show one failure being routed there
Run both services and Kafka with Docker Compose and document how you would scale the consumer
stretch: Add a reconciliation job that finds mismatched balances
Expose consumer lag as a metric

projects.title: Webhook relay with retries in Node and TypeScript
projects.pitch: A service that receives events from one app and reliably delivers them to subscriber endpoints, retrying failures with backoff.
milestones: Define typed event and subscriber models and a request-signing scheme so receivers can verify the sender
Build endpoints to register subscribers and to accept events with schema validation
Deliver events with exponential backoff and a maximum attempt count; show the retry timeline for a failing receiver
Store every delivery attempt so an operator can see status per event
Write tests with a fake receiver that fails twice and then succeeds
Document the delivery guarantee you offer (at least once) and the duplicate handling receivers need
stretch: A replay endpoint for failed events

projects.title: Multilingual product search with Elasticsearch
projects.pitch: Search for a local marketplace where shoppers type in English, Hindi written in English letters, or with typos, and still find products.
milestones: Create a synthetic catalogue of at least 5,000 products and index it with an explicit mapping
Build a search endpoint with relevance scoring across title and description with field boosts
Add typo tolerance and a synonym list (for example chappal and slipper) and show queries that failed before and work now
Add filters and facets for price, category and rating with pagination
Measure relevance on 20 hand-written queries before and after tuning, using a simple table of hits in the top 5
Run Elasticsearch in Docker, document the index settings and explain how you would reindex without downtime
stretch: Transliteration of Hindi words in Devanagari to Roman letters

projects.title: Rate limiter and live leaderboard on Redis
projects.pitch: A small service that protects an API with a rate limiter and serves a live top-10 quiz leaderboard, built to handle bursts.
milestones: Write a one-page design: requests per second you target, data shapes in Redis, and what happens if Redis is down
Implement a token-bucket or sliding-window limiter and show it rejecting a burst with the right status code and retry header
Implement the leaderboard with a sorted set and show rank and top-10 queries
Make updates atomic and prove it with a concurrent load test
Expose metrics (allowed, rejected, latency) and plot them under load
Write the trade-offs: memory use, key expiry, consistency across several app servers
stretch: Per-user and global limits at the same time
Persist leaderboard snapshots to a database every hour

projects.title: Handwritten digit recognizer for Indian scripts
projects.pitch: Train a small convolutional model to recognise handwritten digits in Devanagari or another Indian script and serve it behind an API.
milestones: Choose a public digit dataset, record its licence in the README and show a grid of sample images per class
Build a baseline (for example logistic regression on pixels) and record its accuracy
Train a small convolutional network with augmentation and compare it with the baseline on a held-out set
Show a confusion matrix, list the three most confused digit pairs and view the actual wrong images
Serve the model with an endpoint that accepts an image and returns the top 3 labels with scores; reject non-images
Package with Docker and write down where the model fails (thin strokes, rotated writing) so a user knows its limits
stretch: Export the model to a lighter format and compare speed
Add a confidence threshold that says 'not sure'
